subject: Procurement constraints & billing options — GreenGrid AI follow-up
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Priya Nair <priya@greengrid.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement constraints & billing options — GreenGrid AI follow-up

Hi Priya — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Highlights from the call:
- GreenGrid is evaluating Redwood for inference-hosted (hosted API) and a Reserved/Dedicated path for a pilot (targeting 50–75k tokens/day initially).
- Procurement note flagged: your standard vendor setup currently requires card-based payments for net-new SaaS vendors; POs are generally not permitted unless annual committed spend > $250k.
- You also mentioned Finance may require a prepayment or a vendor onboarding packet for spend > $50k in the first 12 months.

Open questions we need to confirm from your side: 
1) Can you confirm whether the card-only rule is a hard policy or if Procurement would entertain an exception for annual commitments between $50k–$250k? Who is the right person on your side to request an exception?
2) Is AWS Marketplace an acceptable procurement channel for GreenGrid? If so, we can route initial consumption there which would avoid a direct purchase order.
3) If prepay is required, does Finance prefer a single prepay invoice (Redwood issues an invoice; GreenGrid prepays) or a tokenized company card for preauthorization?

From Redwood’s side we can offer the following commercial paths to unblock the pilot quickly:
- Card-based monthly billing (fastest),
- Prepaid credits (invoice + prepay) for the first quarter,
- Marketplace subscription (if GreenGrid approves AWS Marketplace onboarding).

Attached: pricing-sheet-RedwoodDedicated.xlsx and a short SOW template (SOW-template.pdf) you can share with Procurement.

Next steps proposed:
- Priya confirms Procurement/Finance preference and the name(s) for the exception channel,
- If needed, we escalate and provide a completed procurement-exception-template (I can prepare), SOC2 and onboarding docs.

If it helps I can set a 30-minute alignment call that includes your procurement contact + our finance lead (Laura). What time works for you next week?

Thanks — Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment(s): pricing-sheet-RedwoodDedicated.xlsx (spreadsheet), SOW-template.pdf (doc)

From: Priya Nair <priya@greengrid.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: GreenGrid AI Procurement <procurement@greengrid.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement constraints & billing options — GreenGrid AI follow-up

Thanks Sean — good summary. A few clarifications from Procurement/Finance side: 

- Card-only is our default for SaaS vendors under $250k ARR. We do not issue POs to a vendor unless there is a signed master agreement and a committed spend above that threshold. This is a fairly strict policy but there are business exceptions.
- For new vendors, our policy is to require prepayment or vendor credit-check for any projected spend > $50k in the first 12 months. Prepay is preferred if us and the vendor cannot be on net-30 terms immediately.
- AWS Marketplace is being evaluated by our procurement committee; it avoids a lot of onboarding steps but needs approval (we expect a decision in ~2 weeks).

Questions for Redwood: 
1) Can Redwood accept a prepaid invoice (we pay upfront) and then apply credits to usage?
2) If not, would Redwood approve an ACH / company card on file + 30 day terms once our legal completes onboarding?
3) We need SOC2 Type II and a short data residency statement for EU data (GreenGrid has a small portion of customers in EU).

If you can provide the exception template and the SOC2 link (and confirm prepay flow), I will bring all of this back to procurement and finance and try to fast-track an exception or confirm AWS Marketplace.

Best,
Priya Nair
Head of Procurement | GreenGrid AI
priya@greengrid.ai

---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Priya Nair <priya@greengrid.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement constraints & billing options — GreenGrid AI follow-up

Hi Priya — appreciate the clarity. Short answers and proposed workarounds below: 

1) Prepaid invoice: Yes, Redwood supports a prepaid credits model. We can issue an invoice for an agreed amount and apply credits to the account. This is our standard route for pilots where customers want to prepay.

2) ACH / card + net terms: We can accept company card/ACH now; net-30 terms require Finance onboarding and approval. If Finance will accept a company card on file we can start immediately while legal completes onboarding.

3) SOC2 & data residency: SOC2 Type II report available here: https://redwood-inference.s3.amazonaws.com/security/SOC2-report-2025.pdf. We have a short note on data residency (EU data remains in eu-central-1 when requested) — happy to share a one-page statement for your legal team.

Concrete commercial paths to propose to Procurement (I will prepare a short packet):
A) Card-first pilot: immediate start, monthly billing by card, low admin friction.
B) Prepay pilot: GreenGrid prepays a quarter’s estimated spend; credits applied against usage (fast onboarding, reduces collection risk).
C) Marketplace route: If procurement approves AWS Marketplace, we can onboard there and purchases flow through Marketplace billing.

I have attached a procurement-exception-template (procurement-exception-template.pdf) and will draft a short cover note requesting an exception pathway if you think Procurement will be unwilling to accept prepay.

If you’re open, I’ll schedule a 30-minute session next Tue to walk Procurement & Finance through the three options and timelines. Laura — can you join for finance/commercial questions?

Thanks — Sean

---
Attachment(s): procurement-exception-template.pdf
(Links: SOC2 report provided above)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Procurement constraints & billing options — GreenGrid AI follow-up

Laura / Lauren — forwarding the thread with Priya (GreenGrid). Vote of confidence here but Procurement has a hard card-first stance and Finance may ask for prepay for new vendors > $50k.

Action items for us: 
- Laura: can you prepare two short commercial options (A: Card pilot pricing; B: Prepay credits for Q1) with clear timelines and an estimate of seat/throughput pricing so I can attach to the exception packet?
- Lauren: please draft a one-page exception request/cover note that Priya can hand to Procurement that highlights: business case, mitigants (prepay + credits), SOC2 link and data residency note. Use the attached procurement-exception-template.pdf and our standard SOW-template.pdf as an appendix.

Please keep this tight — Priya said procurement decision could come within ~2 weeks if we provide the right paperwork. I’ll offer to run the 30-minute alignment call once we have the packet.

Thanks — Sean

(Internal note: If Procurement refuses all exceptions, fallback is Marketplace — check AWS Marketplace onboarding lead time and whether we can provide an expedited path.)
